rationale: A case describes recurrent allergic symptoms after eating dried fig. The fig-and-olive trial reports one hiccup-related withdrawal without hallucination-frequency data. The Parkinson reports record hallucinations during other clinical exposures. The direction for dried figs and Parkinson visual hallucination frequency remains unresolved.

The rheumatoid arthritis comparison recorded a rise in patient-rated pain after diclofenac withdrawal in the corn-oil arm. The previously cited physician pain estimate belongs to fish oil. Between-oil changes were inconclusive. Osteoarthritis comparator and local procedure pain results leave refined edible corn oil and Parkinson pain unresolved.

Active-comparator trials gave inconclusive fatigue outcomes. The rheumatoid arthritis source measured time until fatigue during analgesic withdrawal, with inconclusive within-arm changes. The Japanese desk-work trial has no public arm results located. Refined corn oil and Parkinson fatigue severity remain unresolved.

A whole dry Ajwa crossover collected an unpublished mood diary. The adjunct schizophrenia trial gives only aggregate negative symptoms, and healthy date studies measured alertness, vigor or stress. Animal movement and preference results differ in preparations and endpoints. Parkinson diet studies have no isolated dried-date apathy comparison.
